name: Nouvelle cuisine
summary: A light French restaurant kitchen. The chef buys fresh produce at the market, cooks fish and vegetables for a short time, makes sauces without flour, and plates each dish in the kitchen. Gault and Millau gave it ten rules in 1973.

philosophy.core_thesis: Take the weight out of Escoffier: fresh market produce, short cooking and a sauce without flour let the taste of the ingredient lead.
design_principles: Buy produce at the market on the day, and write the menu from what you bought.
Cook fish, shellfish and green vegetables for the shortest time: fish stays translucent at the centre, vegetables stay crisp.
Make each sauce from the cooking juices, a reduction and a little cream or butter; leave out the roux.
Keep the menu short: three or four dishes for each course, not a long list.
Plate each dish in the kitchen on a large white plate, one portion for one guest.
Leave about 40 per cent of the plate empty, and cut the garnish to two or three items.
Pair a savoury main ingredient with fruit, a flower or a herb, and keep every flavour clear.
Let the chef follow the season and invent: a new dish each week.
anti_patterns: A heavy sauce thickened with flour and cooked for hours
Game or meat hung until it is high
A long menu with a dish for every taste
Fish and vegetables cooked until grey and soft
A garnish that covers the plate
A dish carved or finished at a trolley beside the table

plating.composition: A small portion arranged by the chef on a wide plate: a fan of thin slices or a neat piece, a pool of sauce beneath, and a few vegetables set apart.
plating.plate: A white round porcelain plate of 280 to 320 mm with a wide flat rim, bigger than a classic dinner plate.
plating.portion: A main piece of 90 to 130 g with 30 to 50 ml of sauce and two small vegetable items; about 55 per cent of the plate is covered.
plating.height: The food stands 15 to 30 mm high; the sauce forms a pool of 2 to 3 mm under the main piece, not a coat over it.
rules: Spoon the sauce onto the plate first and lay the main piece on it.
Fan a thin slice of fish or meat from the middle to the rim, or set a small round piece at the centre.
Cook each vegetable on its own and place it apart: a pile of three or four green beans, a small turned carrot.
Wipe the rim; the plate leaves the pass ready, and no waiter changes it.
Use one herb leaf or one flower as the only decoration.

pantry.rule: Choose the fish, the vegetables and the herbs that the market has that morning, and use cream and butter in small amounts to finish a sauce.

technique.bases: A light fish fumet, a clear veal or chicken stock, and the cooking juices of the dish itself; the cook reduces them and does not use roux.
technique.details: A thin escalope cooked on one side for seconds, a vegetable cooked al dente and shocked in cold water, a sauce mounted with a cube of cold butter, a single herb leaf.

flavour.profile: Fresh and clear: the taste of the fish, the shell or the vegetable first, with sorrel, citrus, herbs and a light butter sauce.
flavour.balance: Acid from sorrel, lemon or vinegar sits against a small amount of cream; salt is low and sweet comes from fruit used with savoury food.
flavour.fat: Butter and cream give about 25 to 40 per cent of the energy of a main dish, less than in the classic kitchen.
flavour.seasoning: Salt and pepper at the end, fresh herbs added at the last moment, a little acid to finish. No long stock with many spices.

palette.strategy: Use a large white plate as an empty field, with pale pink fish, one green and a pale sauce.

service.format: A tasting menu or a short à la carte menu; the plates come from the pass already arranged, and the waiter sets each one in front of the guest.
service.courses: A menu dégustation of five to eight small courses, or an à la carte meal of three courses with a sorbet between.
service.tableware: Large white plates, thin crystal glasses, plain cutlery and white linen without a gold rim.
service.setting: A family restaurant or a country inn with a chef who is the owner, a small brigade of ten to twenty cooks and a dining room of 30 to 50 seats.

dishes.dish: Black truffle soup in a pastry lid
Salad of warm foie gras and green vegetables
Steamed sole with a light butter sauce
Duck with a fruit and vinegar sauce

positive: large white plate with wide rim
thin salmon escalope on pale green sorrel sauce
crisp green beans in a small pile
light butter sauce pooled under the fish

canonical_works.work: The ten commandments of nouvelle cuisine, Le Nouveau Guide

evidence.title: Crayfish escabèche on asparagus gazpacho (Lameloise, Chagny)

emotion.target_response: The relief of a light lunch that still feels like an event: clear taste, a clean plate and no weight after the meal.

use_cases: a menu for a 1970s French restaurant
a food photograph of a small plated dish on a large white plate
a period scene of a chef at the pass
avoid_when: the brief wants a heavy sauced dish from a grand hotel
the brief wants foam, gel or liquid nitrogen
the brief is home or street food

modifiers.how: Steam each item, bind the sauce with fromage blanc or vegetable purée, and cut the fat share to 15 per cent.

modifiers.request: more local and plain, with the produce of one garden
modifiers.how: Keep the market menu, drop the chef's flourishes, and name the farm of each ingredient.
Bring back the demi-glace and the roux, coat the main piece, and add a guéridon service.
